topics.title: 隐私与敏感数据
topics.summary: Public Protection Level P1 data may be entered into AI tools. Entering confidential, personal, or proprietary information (including FERPA student records, unpublished research, or P2–P4 data) is generally prohibited, unless specifically permitted under UC enterprise license agreements and approved protection levels. Instructors are advised not to upload student materials to third-party AI tools lacking a university MOU.

claims.text: Effective January 1, 2026, the UC Berkeley Research Misconduct Policy governs allegations of research misconduct through three standardized stages: assessment, inquiry, and investigation.

evidence.quote: This policy describes the framework UC Berkeley uses to receive, assess, and resolve allegations of research misconduct. It outlines clear definitions, roles, responsibilities, and the three procedural stages—assessment, inquiry, and investigation—designed to ensure thorough, objective, and timely review consistent with federal law and University policy.

claims.text: A finding of research misconduct under UC Berkeley policy requires establishing three criteria: a significant departure from accepted practices of the relevant research community, committed intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly, proven by a preponderance of the evidence.

evidence.quote:
III. REQUIREMENTS FOR FINDINGS OF RESEARCH MISCONDUCT (§ 93.103).
Finding of research misconduct requires:
There be a significant departure from accepted practices of the relevant research community; and
The misconduct be committed intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly; and
The allegation be proven by a preponderance of the evidence standard.

evidence.location: Section III: Requirements for Findings of Research Misconduct; extracted text lines 141-145

claims.text: All collected data, evidence, records, and reports from research misconduct proceedings must be securely maintained for seven (7) years following completion, unless transferred to a research sponsor or released by ORI.

evidence.quote:
The timelines for a written appeal are as follows:
(1) If the administrative resolution does not include a separation status sanction,
the student must submit the written appeal within ten (10) days of the issuance
of the Administrative Resolution Letter.
(2) If the Administrative Resolution includes a separation status sanction, and the
student does not request a formal hearing but wishes to appeal the sanctions,
the student must submit a written intent to appeal the sanctions within five (5)

claims.text: The Graduate Division defines graduate student academic misconduct as distinct from research misconduct (reported through the Vice Chancellor’s Office for Research) and general behavioral misconduct (reported through the Center for Student Conduct).

evidence.quote: Graduate student academic misconduct refers, but is not limited to plagiarism, cheating, fabrication or the facilitation of academic dishonesty by any student, while enrolled in a graduate program. It is different from research misconduct which is fabrication, falsification, or plagiarism, in proposing, performing, or reviewing research, or in reporting research results. Research misconduct is reported through the Vice Chancellor’s Office for Research

claims.text: The Graduate Student Academic Misconduct Policy establishes two resolution phases (early resolution and committee-led investigation) evaluated under the preponderance of the evidence standard (51% likelihood), with a presumption of non-responsibility throughout the process.

evidence.quote:
The Graduate Student Academic Misconduct Policy describes two phases for addressing suspected academic misconduct by graduate and professional students: An early resolution phase and a committee-led investigation phase. Throughout both phases, the Graduate Division serves as an impartial consultant to ensure consistency, equity, and adherence to due process.
All information related to a case is evaluated through the preponderance standard, which means more likely than not, or a 51% likelihood.
evidence.title: Berkeley Graduate Division: Graduate Student Academic Integrity Overview
evidence.location: Graduate Academic Misconduct Policy: Overview & Resolution Phases; extracted text lines 135-136

claims.text: Under the Graduate Student Academic Misconduct Policy, students have the right to appeal within 10 days of receiving the hearing committee’s decision based on new evidence or significant procedural error.

evidence.quote:
Students have a right to appeal (within 10 days of receiving the notification of the hearing committee’s decision), if
A student has new evidence that was not available at the time of the hearing that could affect the committee’s decision.
A student has grounds to believe that there was a significant procedural error that affected the committee’s decision.
evidence.title: Berkeley Graduate Division: Procedures & Resources for Graduate Students
evidence.location: Students' Rights and Responsibilities: Right to appeal; extracted text lines 128-130

claims.text: At UC Berkeley, AI tools procured by individual units must adhere to the approved Protection Level limitations advised by that unit, and units should clearly advise staff and users of the appropriate use and Protection Level limitations of their AI tools.

evidence.quote: Use of AI tools procured by units separately from the campus or systemwide agreements mentioned above must also adhere to the approved Protection Level limitations advised by the unit to ensure compliance with the agreement and appropriate protections relative to the safety features of the tool.
evidence.title: Campus Guidance on the Appropriate Use of Generative AI Tools
evidence.location: OERCS Appropriate Use: Unit-procured tools; extracted text lines 53-53

claims.text: UC Berkeley warns that individuals who accept click-through agreements for AI tools (such as OpenAI and ChatGPT terms of use) without delegated signature authority may face personal liability, including responsibility for compliance with terms and conditions.

evidence.quote: Personal Liability: Please note that certain generative AI tools use click-through agreements. Click-through agreements, including OpenAI and ChatGPT terms of use, are contracts. Individuals who accept click-through agreements without delegated signature authority may face personal consequences, including responsibility for compliance with terms and conditions.
evidence.title: Campus Guidance on the Appropriate Use of Generative AI Tools
evidence.location: OERCS Appropriate Use: Click-through contracts; extracted text lines 71-71

claims.text: UC Berkeley states that units offering AI tools separately from campus or systemwide agreements should clearly advise staff and users of the appropriate use and Protection Level limitations of those tools.

evidence.quote: Units offering such tools should clearly advise staff and users as to the appropriate use and Protection Level limitations of the AI (and all) tools that they offer.
evidence.title: Campus Guidance on the Appropriate Use of Generative AI Tools
evidence.location: OERCS Appropriate Use: Unit tool advice; extracted text lines 53-53

claims.text: UC Berkeley has AI risk assessment pre-screening questions that employees can use to gauge the level of risk involved for an AI use case where AI is integrated into a product, service, or feature at the university. Depending on the risk level determined, the CERC-AIR subcommittee may be engaged for a broader risk assessment.
